say: When welfare code drifts away from the law, the people who depend on it pay. In Telangana, an eligibility algorithm cancelled more than one point eight million food cards, and nobody could check why.
Niyam is an AI agent that reads every new government order and updates the welfare eligibility rules, written as code, by itself. Every rule links back to the exact clause it came from.

This is a real run on the July 2024 amendment to the Ladki Bahin scheme, a Marathi PDF. Niyam decides the order matters, quotes every changed clause, and checks each quote against the document. Claude Code updates the rulebook and writes test citizens at every limit. Then a separate verifier, blind to the code change, writes its own test citizens from the law. Sixteen of sixteen agree.
Click any rule and ask why. You get the clause in Marathi and in English, and exactly which agent, model and session wrote this line.

That answer comes from Entire. Every rule commit carries a checkpoint with the coding agent's full session, open to anyone, no login: the source order, all six changes, the confidence, and the Claude Code conversation that wrote them.
Each change arrives as a pull request with the quotes and the verification. This one removes some people from the scheme, so Niyam does not merge it. It waits for a human.

say: cfo.ai's agent, Ari, turned our measured costs into a thirty six month business plan: about ninety five percent gross margin, and cash flow positive from month twenty one in the base case.
We traced every run with neatlogs, and it flagged the incidents our agent ran into while we built it. Here are three, and how each one was fixed.

Incident one, a runaway loop. The version one trace shows encode, verify and resolve repeating, three dollars on a single document. The trace inputs showed why: the verifier never saw the benefit formula. We added it, plus a loop guard, and the same document now runs straight through.

Incident two, validation errors. neatlogs flagged two calls on our cheaper model that ran for a minute and came back with their answer cut off mid sentence. The fix: when an answer fails validation, retry with more room and less thinking. The agent now recovers by itself.
Incident three, a usage limit. Our model provider's spend cap stopped a job half way. Instead of failing, jobs now pause, and resume from their last good step once the limit is raised.
With every stage traced, we also picked cheaper models wherever the numbers showed no loss. Cost per document fell from eighty eight cents to thirteen, with every check at one hundred percent.

Real documents are messy. Scanned pages, broken model output, and a hidden prompt injection were all handled. From an empty rulebook and only the founding order, Niyam rebuilt the whole scheme and passed all twenty five of our hand written tests.

Anyone can check their eligibility in Marathi, Hindi or English, with the source of every reason, right in the browser. Developers and AI assistants get the same answers through an API and an MCP server.
Niyam. When the law changes, the code changes with it. The links are in the post.
